subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev switching continue adopting arbitrary pre-existing checkouts after remote verification, or must it use only a fresh/OpenClaw-owned checkout?
rationale: Remote verification fixes source selection but cannot establish that repository configuration and hooks are safe; eliminating that execution boundary changes the documented checkout-adoption behavior and requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Require an OpenClaw-owned checkout
options.body: Refuse unowned pre-existing directories and clone into a fresh managed path, closing both foreign-source and executable-Git-config vectors.

options.title: Merge the incremental remote check
options.body: Accept the foreign-source mitigation now while explicitly retaining the known arbitrary Git-config execution boundary for a separately sponsored follow-up.

recommendation.title: Require an OpenClaw-owned checkout
recommendation.body: Refuse unowned pre-existing directories and clone into a fresh managed path, closing both foreign-source and executable-Git-config vectors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects Vincent Koc to the package update and handoff paths affected by this boundary.
